title: Test: Tool Calling
summary: Check what you learned across the whole chapter.

questions.q: The section **Retrying Uncertain Actions** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A mutating tool over an endpoint without deduplication ships actuate, probe, and compensate together, with the probe written before dispatch against a captured baseline.

A shared tool protocol cuts integration to N_host + N_tool adapters, but listed tools supply only interface syntax: descriptions are untrusted input and admitted schemas must be bound to the server instance.

A logical operation ID names one intended effect across attempts, each attempt gets a fresh attempt ID, and the ID is safe only under an endpoint contract that binds it to caller, scope, and arguments.
A schema settles only structure, so any precondition that depends on current state (an expected version, a canonical path) must be enforced atomically with the effect at the endpoint.
